newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Unknown firm wins 5 pct Russia's LUKoil in tender.
newsitem.headline: Unknown firm wins 5 pct Russia's LUKoil in tender.

text.p: Unknown company LUKoil-Reserve-Invest won a tender for a five percent stake in Russia's largest oil company LUKoil, LUKoil said in a press release on Friday.

LUKoil-Reserve-Invest bid 251 billion roubles ($43.6 million) for the stake -- the highest bid of all companies participating in the tender and above the starting price of 250 billion roubles, LUKoil said.

"We are happy with the fact that the winner was LUKoil-Reserve-Invest," the release quoted LUKoil Vice President Leonid Fedun as saying. LUKoil-Reserve-Invest is a member of Russia's National Association of Participants of the Stock Market (PAUFOR).
"This company will be able to fully carry out its responsibility with regard to the conditions of the investment tender," Fedun said.

The winner of the tender must hand over to LUKoil 15 percent of shares in OAO Nizhnevolzhskneft, a subsidiary of LUKoil, and acquire and deliver oil equipment worth $100 million by the end of 1997 to the Caspian Sea.

LUKoil is the prize in Russia's struggling oil sector, producing 58.5 million tonnes of oil (1.17 million barrels per day) in 1996, up two percent from 1995. It has an aggressive overseas exploration policy and is working on increasing its oil refining capacity.
